## Resolution decision — moved to epic b575

This bug describes a structural duplication that is on-scope for epic b575-ac1c-f720-4839 ("Cycle-end arbiter + workflow unification (BLOCK/DEFER/DROP rulings, max_cycles, parity local+PR)"), not an orthogonal CI cleanup. Two PR-side workflows running ci-llm-review-runner.sh against the same SHA break several epic invariants:

- cycle-ledger integrity (story 5621 will wire runner.py to write cycle-ledger.json → two ledger entries per SHA → cycle_num and cross_cycle_pattern undefined)
- arbiter dispatch dedup (cycle-end arbiter already on main from story b1b6) — duplicate dispatch yields duplicate orphan-task tickets and duplicate defense-store rows
- review.max_cycles enforcement (story 35b8, merged) — effective cap becomes 2 * max_cycles
- SC10 E2E PR validation (story c4f1) — "the arbiter fired on a real PR" is ambiguous when two runs exist
- Parity local+PR (epic SC) — local has 1 entry point (/dso:commit → /dso:review); PR currently has 2

Decision: rather than fixing this as a standalone bug, the work is captured as a new story under epic b575, slotted between story 35b8 (max_cycles config, closed) and story 5621 (CI runner wiring). 5621 depends_on this new story so its cycle-ledger writes land on a single canonical PR-side pipeline.

The required check stays `llm-review` per required-checks.txt; the branch ruleset still enforces it; coverage of "no merge without LLM review" is preserved mathematically (the canonical run is the same — we only remove the duplicate run, not the required run).

Closing this bug as MOVED — work tracked under the new story (linked below).
